summary.tldr: Creates a national process for recognizing some military service as wartime service and for listing and reviewing Canadian Armed Forces operations.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of National Defence to develop a national framework with objective criteria for wartime service and with symbolic and commemorative ways to recognise it.
Requires consultations with veterans, veterans’ groups, non-Canadian Armed Forces personnel who served alongside Canadian forces, military history experts, and others the minister chooses.
Requires the minister to table the framework in Parliament within one year and publish it on the Department of National Defence website.

Requires the Governor in Council, on the minister’s recommendation, to designate military service as wartime service when it meets the framework’s criteria, including a first review of Canadian Armed Forces operations from July 27, 1953 to the framework’s tabling.
Requires the minister to keep a public searchable list of Canadian Armed Forces operations, update it when operations start or change, and publish the minister’s recommendations and reasons.
States that a wartime service designation does not create any new financial benefit a member or veteran does not already have under another Act of Parliament.
summary.background: The bill says it would create a national framework for recognising military service as wartime service. It also sets out a process for reviewing past and new Canadian Armed Forces operations.
